simple.meaning: חָתַל (châthal) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to swathe.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 2 times across Ezekiel, beginning at Ezekiel 16:4. Its contexts include birth.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חָתַל (H2853).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: חָתַל (châthal) / H2853 is traced through Ezekiel 16:4 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: As for your birth, in the day you were born your navel was not cut. You weren’t washed in water to cleanse you. You weren’t salted at all, nor wrapped in blankets at all.

definitions.full: H2853. chathal [ חָתַל ] verb perhaps entwine, enwrap (possibly denominative, so MV and others; yet compare Late Hebrew חוֺתָל woven date-basket ) — Pu`al Perfect 2feminine singular חֻתַּלְתְּ and Hoph`al Infinitive absolute הָחְתֵּל be swathed, swaddled ; — חֻתַּלְתְּ לֹא וְהָחְתֵּל הֻמְלַ֫חַתְּ לֹא וְהָמְלֵחַ Ezek 16:4 and not at all wast thou rubbed with salt, and not at all wast thou swaddled , of Jerusalem under figure of infant.
